text:
jordan-support: Heads-up — AcmeRetail hit a sudden wave of 429s during their nightly ingest (approx 2026-03-16 00:12:10 -> 00:18:45 UTC). They sent a couple example request IDs but asked us to help gather repro evidence. Asking for HAR/curl + headers so we can map to quota windows.

sam-runtime: Thanks. Can you paste the first/last request-id they saw and the model/route they hit? Also whether they use streaming or non-streaming calls.

jordan-support: Customer excerpt: "we see 429 responses with header X-Request-Id: req-1791122334-6b2a and req-1791122399-b9f4, roughly every ~2s from 3 workers for ~6 minutes. Non-streaming /v1/outputs with model=redwood/embedding-7b (batching disabled)."

irina-sre: @sam-runtime fyi check both per-minute and burst token buckets. It smells like a short burst that exhausted their burst quota then fell back to per-minute enforcement. Ask for the response headers (x-rate-limit-limit, x-rate-limit-remaining, x-rate-limit-reset or our x-rw-headers). Those will confirm.

jordan-support: Pasted a raw 429 response the customer forwarded: 

```
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
Content-Type: application/json
X-Request-Id: req-1791122334-6b2a
x-rate-limit-limit: 120
x-rate-limit-remaining: 0
x-rate-limit-reset: 00:13:15
{
  "error": {"type":"rate_limit","message":"quota exceeded"}
}
```

sam-runtime: Good. Can we get them to run a minimal curl that reproduces the 429 and include the exact request id? Share this snippet with them (remove their API key when pasting publicly):

```
curl -v -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/outputs \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <REDACTED>" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -H "x-request-id: req-1791122399-b9f4" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood/embedding-7b","input":"test payload","stream":false}'
```

irina-sre: Also ask them for a HAR from the browser or an httpdump from one worker for the 00:12:00-00:20:00 UTC window. If they can't produce a HAR, a curl loop with sleep and gcd of timestamps will work. We need: first request ts, last request ts, inter-request interval, and headers for 5-10 429s.

ratebot: alert: rate_limit_spike detected for customer AcmeRetail at 2026-03-16T00:13:12Z — peak QPS 28, sustained 6m.

jordan-support: Customer provided a short timeline and a few more IDs: 
- 2026-03-16T00:12:10Z req-1791122334-6b2a -> 200
- 2026-03-16T00:12:45Z req-1791122399-b9f4 -> 429
- 2026-03-16T00:13:18Z req-1791122410-c2d1 -> 429
- 2026-03-16T00:18:40Z req-1791122748-d0e7 -> 200

sam-runtime: That looks like a burst then graceful recovery when tokens freed. Two quick asks for reproducibility artifacts we need from the customer:
1) HAR or tcpdump for the 00:12-00:19 UTC window.
2) The exact curl from one of their workers that produced req-1791122399-b9f4 (so we can replay). If they cannot share API key, ask them to run the curl locally with an x-request-id we provide and send back the verbose output including response headers.

irina-sre: If they give us the HAR, we should extract the sequence of x-rate-limit-* headers and plot remaining over time to confirm bucket exhaustion. If only headers are available, ask for at least 10 consecutive 429 responses with headers.

jordan-support: Sent steps back to customer: 1) run the curl above 10x with a unique x-request-id each time and attach the full -v output, 2) export HAR for 00:11:30-00:19:30, 3) tell us if they use any client-side retry/backoff (it looked like their workers retried every ~2s).

sam-runtime: Also ask them to tell us which subscription tier / quota plan they are on and whether they changed any autoscaling or concurrency settings on their side. Could be parallel workers + small quota window.

jordan-support: Customer replied they are on "Standard" reserved capacity with a soft burst of 120/min and 60/s smoothing. They said they run 3 parallel ingest workers each sending ~8 req/s for short bursts. They will upload HAR and a debug bundle.

irina-sre: Once we have HAR + one verbose curl with X-Request-Id and full response headers, I'll correlate against our ingress logs and bucket counters. If we confirm it's a customer-side parallelism spike, we should recommend smoothing or increasing burst commit. If it's our routing error, escalate to runtime infra.

jordan-support: Action items: @sam-runtime to validate endpoint logs for the provided request ids and return timelines. @irina-sre to prepare quick script to parse HAR for x-rate-limit headers. I'll keep customer coordinated and collect the HAR + curl outputs. :thumbsup: 

sam-runtime: Got it — will pull logs for req-1791122334-6b2a, req-1791122399-b9f4, req-1791122410-c2d1 and post back in ~20m.

irina-sre: I'll draft the HAR parser now and post link to gist.

jordan-support: Thanks team, I'll update thread when I have the HAR.
